messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: hosted-runtime kvcache memory alarm on pool hosted-prod — sustained KV map growth and >70% OOM probability on model-x workloads. Trigger: continuous-batching controller alert. Paging @eng-sre @eng-runtime @product.
morgan: seeing client errors 504/502 for streaming endpoints. GPUs healthy in CPU but a cluster subset shows steadily increasing GPU mem graph. Notable: long-lived sessions from a few tenants.
tara: matching customer reports: 'responses stall then drop' from 3 accounts. They send very long prompts + heavy prefixing. Could be accumulation + prefetch.
devin: looking at metrics now. KV map per-shard spike started ~00:42 UTC after the throughput rollout that increased batching to 900ms. Continuous-batching + prefetch seems to amplify retained KV state for sessions.
nina: collected traces: lots of sessions with "session_state.size" increasing between requests. 95p token latency rising. Also seeing evict failures: `evict() -> busy-lock` in logs.
cs-raj: customers notified to CS triage. Two enterprise accounts on dedicated routes impacted more severely.
devin: propose immediate mitigation (ordered):
1) revert batching window to 150ms via FF for hosted-prod routes (low risk).
2) enable session-length caps at proxy layer (max_tokens_in_session=120k) to prune runaway histories.
3) temporarily disable prefetch for hosted model-x instances for 20m.
4) patch kvcache eviction thresholds to be more aggressive (lower low-watermark) and roll to 20% canary.
5) if memory not stabilizing, spin +4 nodes in hosted-prod pool for 30m.
morgan: rolling FF to revert batch window now: `infractl feature set continuous_batch_window_ms=150 --env hosted-prod`

deploybot: Feature-flag change started: roll to 25 nodes (https://deploys.redwood/internal/99821).

tara: disabling prefetch for model-x: `infractl runtime set prefetch=false --pool hosted-prod --model model-x`

nina: canary metrics: within 90s of batch-window revert we see queue depth drop and median latency reduce ~140ms. KV growth rate decreasing but some shards still large.
morgan: applying session-length cap at proxy: `proxyctl set session.max_tokens 120000 --route hosted` (temporary). This will issue soft-trim notifications to sessions.
devin: deploying eviction tune to 20% canary now. Patch snippet:
```
kvcache:
  eviction:
    policy: lru
    low_watermark_mb: 256
    high_watermark_mb: 1536
    aggressive_trim: true
```

nina: logs showing fewer lock-contention evict failures after canary. One worker still logs repeated trim-timeout, planning restart.
morgan: restarting runtime-worker-17 in hosted-prod. Node recovered, memory freed.
cs-raj: update to customers: short blurb sent with mitigation steps and estimated 2h follow-up. No customer data lost; behavior was timeouts and degraded throughput.
pm-luca: question: do we want a temporary autoscale hold to avoid dropping capacity while we collect heap dumps?
devin: yes, spinning +4 nodes now: `infractl scale runtime hosted-prod +4` for 30m.
oncall: autoscale action in progress.

nina: after full rollout of eviction tweak and session caps, cluster memory usage trending back to baseline in 12 minutes. Error rate down to normal.
morgan: capturing heapdumps and session snapshots for top offending session IDs for RCA.
devin: RCA owners: @devin (runtime), @tara (observability), @morgan (infra). Postmortem ETA 72h, include experiment data for batch window tradeoffs and a guardrail plan (auto-throttle long sessions + model-specific batching limits).
oncall: incident severity downgraded. Handoff: @devin will monitor for next 2 hours, then rotate to normal oncall. Please collect pre/post metrics for following keys: kvcache.size_by_shard, batch.window_ms, prefetch.request_rate, evict.attempts_failed.
cs-raj: three impacted customers received recovery note; two asked for a remediation timeline to avoid recurrence. Product and CS to coordinate.
pm-luca: flag to product: avoid rolling broad continuous-batching increases without per-model limits and canary guards.
devin: quick follow-ups: 1) add session trimming background job to discard >30k tokens from oldest history for idle sessions, 2) add prefetch backoff when session token count > threshold, 3) add an autoscale-when-kvmem-high policy.

nina: verifying logs for regression: found that the prefetch path didn't check session token count; it would prefetch whole prefix. New fix will add guard.
morgan: thanks all. handoff to @devin for post-recovery monitoring. I'll update the incidents page with short timeline and commands executed. :white_check_mark:
